title: Aug 26 Results + Aug 27 Preview: When the Model Gets Hot
summary: 11-4 on Aug 26 with 73% accuracy—here's what worked and tomorrow's top pick

content.value:
## When Everything Clicks

Here's the thing about August 26th—it was one of those nights where you could feel the momentum building with each result that came in. An 11-4 record with 73.3% accuracy isn't just good; it's the kind of performance that reminds you why we trust the numbers, even when they whisper instead of shout.

## The Standouts

The Padres pick at 68% confidence was our strongest call of the night, and it delivered. There's something satisfying about watching a high-confidence pick play out exactly as predicted—Pittsburgh never really had a chance in that one.

The Phillies-Mariners matchup was another beauty. At 61% confidence, we leaned into Philadelphia's road prowess, and they showed up when it mattered. Sometimes the model sees things before they become obvious.

## The Misses Tell a Story Too

Let's talk about what didn't work. The Tigers upset at 51% confidence? That's basically a coin flip, and the coin landed the other way. The Sox-Marlins miss at 61% stings a bit more, but that's baseball—sometimes the underdog finds their moment.

The Nationals loss is particularly interesting because we're going right back to that well tomorrow. The model doesn't hold grudges, and neither should we.

## Looking Ahead to August 27

Tomorrow's top pick takes us back to Washington, where the Nationals host the Rockies in a rematch situation. Jake Irvin gets the ball for Washington against Colorado's Gabriel Hughes, and here's where it gets interesting—the model is giving us a 50% edge, which is essentially saying these teams are dead even on paper.

But we're still leaning Nationals, and there's a reason for that.

content.title: ⭐ Tomorrow's Top Pick - Aug 27
content.sub: 50% confidence · Jake Irvin vs Gabriel Hughes · Home advantage matters

content.value:
## The Pitcher Matchup

Jake Irvin has been steady at home this season, and Gabriel Hughes is still finding his footing at the big league level. When you've got two teams this evenly matched, the starting pitching becomes the tiebreaker, and Washington holds that edge.

The Rockies away from Coors Field are a different animal—in the worst way possible. Their offense loses its altitude-assisted pop, and suddenly those hitters who look dangerous in Denver become very hittable everywhere else.

50% confidence might not scream "lock of the century," but it's an honest assessment of a game that could genuinely go either way. We're trusting the home field, the pitching matchup, and the fact that Colorado hasn't figured out how to win on the road.

Let's see if Washington can deliver the second time around.
